sum: A ten-day circuit from the Jumla airstrip through the old Khasa capital of Sinja to Rara Lake at 2,990 m, returning over the Ghurchi Lagna and Danphe Lagna passes.

guide.note: The Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers to hire a licensed guide since April 2023, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. Here a guide is practical as well as official: trails braid between villages without signs, very few people speak English, and food and beds have to be arranged house by house.

access: Fly from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, spend the night, and take a morning flight to Jumla. Flights depend on the weather and are often delayed. Jumla is also on the Karnali Highway from Surkhet, a long and rough journey by bus or jeep that still runs when aircraft cannot.

photo.a: The deep blue Rara Lake lies among dark pine-forested hills, with a long line of snow-covered mountains across the horizon.
photo.c: Rara Lake below the Kanjiroba range

includes: Rara National Park permit and TIMS card
lodge, homestay or tent nights and meals on the trek
domestic flights in some packages, road transport in others (confirm)

permits.name: Rara National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park entry posts on the way to the lake, or in advance at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Flights from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj and on to Jumla, and the same back
tips: Draw cash in Kathmandu or Nepalgunj. Jumla has banks and the occasional working cash machine, but do not rely on them.
Bring snacks, tea, coffee and some staples from Nepalgunj or Jumla; village shops sell little beyond noodles and biscuits.
A tent gives you the freedom to stop where the day ends. If you rely on lodges and homestays, let your guide send word ahead.
Try Jumla's red marsi rice and, from September, the local apples.
Keep your park permit handy; park and army posts at the lake and on the trail ask to see it.

days.t: Fly to Jumla, walk to Chere Chaur
days.note: After the morning flight from Nepalgunj, leave the bazaar and climb steadily north through fields and pine to the wide meadows of Chere Chaur. You gain nearly 700 m on arrival day, so go slowly; if the flight is late, sleep in Jumla instead and add a day.
why: A jump from 150 m to sleep at 3,055 m in a single day.

days.t: Chere Chaur to Chalachaur over the Jaljala pass
days.note: Climb through pine and birch to the open top of the Jaljala at about 3,580 m, cross the high pasture of Jaljala Chaur, where horses graze in summer, and descend to the village of Chalachaur.
Downhill through forest and scattered farms to the Sinja Khola and the old capital of the Khasa kings. Spend the afternoon at the Kanakasundari temple and the remains of the old palace site nearby.
North up a side valley past water mills and small villages, climbing gradually into forest. Ghorosingha is a clearing with room to camp and little else, so carry what you need from Sinja.

Climb to the wooded ridge south-west of the lake, where the water first comes into view, then descend to its outlet near Murma and follow the shore round to the park headquarters and the lodges on the northern side.

days.t: Day at Rara Lake and Murma Top
days.note: The climb to Murma Top takes about three hours from the western end of the lake and gives the only view of the whole of it, with the peaks of Mugu and Humla behind. If you would rather rest, walk a section of the shore path instead.

Leave the lake over a low forested ridge, drop to Jhyari and continue through terraced villages to Pina on the main Jumla trail. The road to Gamgadhi runs close by, so expect some dust and the odd tractor.

days.t: Pina to Bumra over the Ghurchi Lagna
days.note: A climb of about 1,000 m through pine, spruce and rhododendron to the Ghurchi Lagna, then down past the national park post at Bhulbule and the houses of Chautha to Bumra. The motor road crosses the same ridge and the trail meets it in places.

days.t: Bumra to Jumla over the Danphe Lagna
days.note: The longest day. Drop to the Sinja Khola, climb for three hours or more through forest to the Danphe Lagna, then descend through Chere Chaur to Jumla. Many groups split it with a night below the pass.
Morning flight to the plains, with a connection to Kathmandu the same day if all goes to plan. If aircraft are grounded for long, the road to Surkhet is the way out.
